title: Microsoft Teams: expanded Markdown support in the compose box
summary: Hold pending narrow corrections to the governance advice. The notice does not place Preview message in the Actions and apps menu, and the briefing overstates what the absence of a Markdown-specific policy proves about existing messaging restrictions. The licensing section should also state the published Teams licence requirement rather than leaving entitlement entirely unknown.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this user-facing compose-box feature.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no licence statement specific to this compose feature is published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the notes and the sentence 'The licence entitlement for this feature is therefore not yet published' with 'Each user in the organisation must have a Teams licence before they can use Teams, except for joining meetings anonymously. No licence requirement specific to Markdown compose mode is published as of November 2026.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Keep the open question narrowly about any requirement beyond the existing Teams entitlement.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Because no messaging policy setting for this feature is documented, administrators cannot confine the mode to a pilot group by policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Markdown messaging policy Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy compose admin setting; Teams Markdown tenant disable compose mode. Read messaging policy settings and the full cmdlet reference; no text establishes this categorical impossibility.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with 'No Markdown-specific messaging policy setting is documented at the time of writing (November 2026), so a policy-scoped pilot of this mode is not documented.' This reports the verified documentation gap without asserting that policy restriction is impossible.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing messaging policy settings do not govern or restrict use of this feature.
claims.quote: Determines whether a user is allowed to chat. Set this to TRUE to allow a user to chat across private chat, group chat and in meetings. Set this to FALSE to prohibit all chat.
claims.fix: Replace 'and none of them governs Markdown mode. Existing messaging policy settings therefore do not stand in for a switch over this feature, and you cannot rely on them to restrict it' with 'but it lists no setting that switches Markdown mode separately from other messaging capabilities.' General chat restrictions remain documented; the verified gap is a separate mode switch, not the absence of all restrictions.
